Thanks again for the quick demo last week. We're on a tight timeline to launch a 6-week pilot with MedixHealth clinical triage, and Compliance has insisted on two requirements before we go live: 1) all inference must remain within EU regions, and 2) the model variant must be pinned — no automatic fallback to other variants or regions.

Key context: this pilot will process PHI-adjacent data (pseudonymized) and the customer requires contractual language and a technical guarantee that inference will not route outside EU. They understand the availability trade-offs but need that guarantee for regulatory sign-off. Pilot target start: 2026-06-01.

Can your team confirm whether Redwood can support a time-boxed forced model selection + region lock (EU only) and what the operational trade-offs would be (downtime risk, perf impact, estimated cost uplift)? Also, what evidence (audit logs / config snapshots) can we provide for the contract addendum? Attached is their security questionnaire.

Appreciate any guidance — cc'd procurement and legal from Medix.

Thanks for the context. Short answers up front: yes, technically doable, but there are operational constraints and we should make the change as controlled as possible. Details below.

1) Approach (recommended):
- Create a routing policy for the Medix pilot that: 1) restricts candidate hosts to EU regions only; 2) forces selection of an explicit model alias (pinned-<model>-vX). That ensures no cross-region routing and no automatic fallback to cheaper or different variants.
- Deploy behind a canary window: start with a small reserved pool (Dedicated or isolated tenancy) to validate perf under load, then expand.

2) Trade-offs and risk:
- No-fallback increases outage blast radius: if the pinned model or EU pool is unhealthy, requests will error rather than hitting a fallback. We can mitigate with canary + alerting + short maintenance windows.
- Cost uplift: expect ~18-30% per-token cost increase due to forced placement and reduced ability to use cheaper variants or opportunistic routing.

3) Technical prerequisites:
- Kernel/quantization compatibility check for the pinned model variant on EU hardware — infra needs to validate.
- Need a dedicated alias and a gating flag in routing logic. This requires a small infra change and a config rollout.

4) Audit/evidence we can provide:
- Time-series of routing decisions (request -> chosen host/model) for the pilot period.
- Periodic config snapshot files and signed change logs.
- KMS-backed key IDs for any encryption in transit/storage, and request-level metadata for region and model id.

5) Next steps / ETA:
- Please open a Jira (INF-4821) with target: infra validation + config change by 2026-05-12, canary week 2026-05-20, pilot GTM 2026-06-01.
- I'll tag infra and runtime owners on the ticket.

Questions for Medix:
- Is a hard no-fallback absolute or would they accept a documented manual failover path (requires contractual language and approvals)?
- Estimated request QPS and latency SLOs for pilot?

I'll follow up with a short technical note.

—Karthik

From a security/compliance perspective we can support this, but we need to lock down and document several items before we provide a contractual guarantee:

Required items before sign-off:
- Signed data processing addendum confirming EU-only processing and the acceptance of the operational trade-offs. Legal needs to review the precise failure semantics.
- Audit artifacts we can produce: per-request routing decision logs, KMS key IDs for any at-rest metadata, and weekly config snapshots.
- Access control: ensure pilot team and Medix have the minimal set of service accounts and that logs shown to them are redacted for other customers.

Technical controls to implement:
- Route-level audit logging with immutable storage (we can hand over CSV snapshots) — infra needs to implement retention policy and export job.
- Ensure keys are in EU KMS and that any snapshots do not contain PII.

I attached our minimal data handling spec to highlight constraints. Legal will need the actual contract language; I recommend we propose a time-limited addendum for the pilot (30–60 days) with a monthly review.

David
Head of Security & Compliance
